title: Meeting Readers and Writers
content: On Friday night I presentedDinotopia: Journey to Chandarato a coed private school in the Hudson Valley. Since they were high school students, most of them were not familiar with the original Dinotopia books. But since the new story is a stand-alone sequel, they could become aquainted with the world of Dinotopia without any other introduction.Then on Saturday I joined a group signing atBooks of Wonder, one of New York City’s favorite children’s bookstores. Owner Peter Glassman billed the event as “three generations of fantasy authors.”I sat beside film-producer-turned-novelist Perry Moore, whose first novelHerohas just been published, andSusan Cooper, whose novelThe Dark is Risingnovel has just been adapted into the live-action filmSeeker: Dark is Rising, released Friday night.The day ended at my hometown bookstore,Oblong Booksin Rhinebeck, New York. I felt so grateful to begin the tour at the place that gave both of my sons their summer jobs, surrounded by so many friends and many of the models for the characters in my new book.
